extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to Remote Code Execution — Full remote code execution on the server process. An attacker can execute arbitrary Python code, read any file the server process can access, exfiltrate environment variables and secrets, and potentially pivot to other systems. [verified: The username query parameter from GET / (line 8) is concatenated unsanitized into a Jinja2 template string at line 12 via from_string('Welcome ' + username + '!').render() with zero validation, escaping, or sandboxing — a fresh unrestricted Environment() is created, and no middleware, decorator, or any other control intercepts this path.]

Denial of Service via expensive template expressions — Server crash or unresponsiveness due to memory exhaustion or CPU saturation. An attacker can repeatedly trigger expensive template rendering to make the service unavailable. [verified: The same unsanitized username-to-template injection path at line 12 accepts arbitrary Jinja2 expressions with no input size limits, no rendering timeout, no rate-limiting, and no resource quotas anywhere in the application or its minimal configuration, allowing CPU/memory exhaustion without needing the RCE gadget chain.]

Reflected XSS via unsanitized username in HTML response — Attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser context, enabling session theft, credential phishing, or page defacement. [verified: The username query parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string rendered with autoescape=False (the default), and the output is returned as HTMLResponse with no sanitization, validation, middleware, or escaping — an attacker supplying ?username=<script>alert(1)</script> will have the payload pass through Jinja2 unchanged and execute in the victim's browser.]
